thesis: Real alternatives, material conditions and institutional power must inform responsibility without erasing personal agency.

ideas.statement: Poverty changes available resources but does not define a person as blameworthy or incapable.
Emergency assistance need not await innocence, while safety conditions and program evaluation remain legitimate.
Employers must provide effective reporting and authority rather than rely on unprotected worker heroism.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Housing First evidence supports bounded housing stability findings, not a cure for every difficulty.
Ordinary competent work can express care for strangers.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Risk allegations require investigation, not an unlimited employee veto.

audit.notes: All assigned units read. Claims remain bounded; hypothetical cases are not empirical evidence.
